description: A cybersecurity-focused student who is mathematically strong and comfortable with theory but feels significant anxiety about the transition from high-level languages to C and low-level memory management.

nodes.description: An introduction to C programming concepts and manual memory management specifically tailored for OS-level development.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This node provides foundational programming context for a student with no_prior_exposure to systems-level languages like C.
nodes.title: C Programming for Systems
Hardware-Software Interface Basics
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential hardware background is provided to bridge the gap for students starting with no_prior_exposure to computer architecture.
nodes.description: Overview of the hardware/software interface, including CPU registers and hardware interrupts.
Detailed exploration of the transition between user mode and kernel mode via system calls.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Targeted scaffolding for no_prior_exposure students to clarify how protection boundaries work in a modern OS.
nodes.title: Understanding Dual-Mode Operation

nodes.personalizationRationale: This is a core required node covering foundational structures that all students must master for the midterm.
nodes.title: OS Foundations & System Structure
nodes.description: Core examination of OS services, system structures, and the Silberschatz model of OS design.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Foundational process management concepts required for the first programming project, relevant to students with no_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Processes and Operations
nodes.description: Study of the process abstraction, including the Process Control Block (PCB) and process state transitions.

nodes.personalizationRationale: IPC is a core syllabus requirement that bridges theoretical process management with practical networking and system design.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC)
nodes.description: Mechanism of Inter-Process Communication using shared memory, message passing, and sockets.
Understanding multithreading models, thread libraries (Pthreads), and implicit threading techniques.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Thread management is a critical requirement for building concurrent OS modules in subsequent course projects.
nodes.title: Threads & Threading Models

nodes.description: Analysis of CPU scheduling criteria and evaluation of algorithms like Round Robin and Multi-Level Feedback Queues.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
nodes.personalizationRationale: Quantitative modeling of scheduling is a core objective that will be tested on the midterm exam.

nodes.title: Midterm Review (Ch. 1-5)
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory assessment node to ensure the student with no_prior_exposure is prepared for the 20% weight midterm exam.
nodes.description: Structured review of Chapters 1-5 material, including practice problems on processes, threads, and scheduling.

nodes.title: Process Synchronization Tools
nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a mandatory core topic essential for the final exam and Project 3 deliveries.
nodes.description: Introduction to the critical-section problem and synchronization tools like Mutexes and Semaphores.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Application of theory to practical system problems is a primary learning objective for all students.
nodes.title: Classic Problems of Synchronization
nodes.description: Solving classic problems like Bounded-Buffer, Readers-Writers, and the Dining Philosophers.

nodes.title: Deadlock Detection & Avoidance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Deadlock management is a required floor topic that scales to the week 12 schedule requirements.
nodes.description: Methods for deadlock characterization, prevention, detection, and avoidance (Banker's Algorithm).

nodes.title: Main Memory & Paging
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core memory management concepts required for understanding how hardware and software interact in address translation.
nodes.description: Deep dive into physical memory addressing, contiguous allocation, and paging structures.

nodes.title: Virtual Memory Management
nodes.personalizationRationale: Virtual memory is a heavily project-relevant topic that all students must master for the final project delivery.
nodes.description: Concepts of virtual memory, demand paging, and the evaluation of page replacement algorithms.
Study of I/O subsystems, performance tradeoffs, and the implementation of file systems.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Capstone block covering the final set of required topics before the cumulative final exam.
nodes.title: I/O Systems & File Storage

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory assessment checkpoint to prepare the student for the 40% weight cumulative final exam.
nodes.title: Final Review (Cumulative)
nodes.description: Cumulative review session covering all course content from OS foundations to file systems.
